inputs.name: Pencil2

symbols.Pencil2::Pencil2: VA 0x59880, size 492; constructor submits advanced setting 14; size 0.228f, color 0xff000000
symbols.Pencil2::GetStrokeDrawableGL: VA 0x59d6c, size 668; settings 1..14 map to GLV1..GLV5,GLV4,GLV7..GLV14 (version 6 maps GLV4; no GLV6)

symbols.Pencil2StrokeDrawableGLV14::calculateDra: VA 0x745a0; configured color or rainbow color
symbols.Pencil2StrokeDrawableRTV4::Init: VA 0x984ac; uses Pencil2StrokeShaderV3 and raw color blend (0,6,7), alpha blend (0,1,7); 150x150 texture init
symbols.g_pointPtn: size 30000; separate 100x300 data reshaped to 3x100x100 atlas

inputs.native_evidence: Default app constructor selects setting 14; default v14 GL renderer owns RTv4 + shader V3, with independent 150x150 grain and 3-tile point atlas. g_backgroundPtn differs from Pencil3 bytes; Pencil2 does not reuse Pencil3's 921600-byte brush atlas. Shader source is embedded around file offset 0x3ebd5 and samples sampler0.r grain, sampler1.r point mask, orientation/taper, width alpha, per-point RGB. Raw blend enum semantics remain unresolved. No native output pixels captured.

inputs.name: Pencil3 comparison
inputs.comparison: Pencil3 g_backgroundPtn SHA256 171b3fc88b6e693a06676bcf0e8029cdc122d50bbeb9f03fe969b153104d3994; g_penPtn is 921600 bytes. Pencil2's texture bytes/sizes differ.

native_capture_plan: On exact app build/device, directly instantiate Pencil2 with setting 14; first read back native RGBA at 1x scale over fixed white/transparent background for deterministic timed multi-point saved and live strokes, pressure ramp, tilt/orientation and size-level changes; compare black and colored/partial-opacity runs. Then sweep settings 1..14 to capture each distinct GL class (settings 6 and 8 share GLV4 per selector). Capture Pencil's selected GLV1 using same sample. Record per-frame advanced settings, point/time/pressure/tilt/orientation/size-level, dimensions, color/alpha, blend state, and exact screenshots/readback. Native visual parity remains unverified until these paired pixels exist.
